source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Complete alertness with fairly mild, barely noticeable forgetfulness, a picture more consistent with an earlier grade","B":"Marked confusion, somnolence, but still arousable to stimuli, representing significant impairment","C":"Fairly few detectable symptoms at all, a picture more consistent with a much earlier stage of encephalopathy","D":"A deep coma state that remains unresponsive to any stimuli, a picture more consistent with Grade 4 than Grade 3"}}
source_row.rationale: Grade 3 hepatic encephalopathy (on the West Haven grading scale) typically presents with marked confusion and somnolence, though the client remains arousable to stimuli, representing significant impairment distinct from the milder Grades 1-2 or the deep coma of Grade 4.
source_row.source_name: AASLD — West Haven Hepatic Encephalopathy Grading
